restrictions: Messages are 271-byte strings M0||X: a uniformly random 136-byte first block M0 and a 135-byte second-block message X. The final padded block is X||0x86, so p = 8 bits are fixed in the final block plus the 512 capacity bits.

Complete SHA3-256 sponge from the all-zero state with prefix rounds 0-4 (RC[0..4]) in both permutation calls, 0x06/0x80 padding, and the full 256-bit digest. No free-start, truncation or raw-permutation shortcut.

Method: the 2-round linear connector and hard-wired trail core No. 3 of Guo et al. (J. Cryptology 33, 2020; ePrint 2019/147), adapted from p = 4 to p = 8 with random first blocks. Step P accepts only core No. 3 by fingerprint (not global min over an unreproduced set). Hard work budget: connector attempts stop at 23 * mu = 2^51.485 units, at most 1024 successful spaces enumerated at 2^32 pairs each. Trail-core generation and extensions are charged preprocessing. The stated time is this cap, not an expected time.
Derived heuristic estimate, not an executed attack. No byte-aligned colliding pair exists yet, the certificate manifest is empty, and no experiment is declared.

Costs are charged in units of one 5-round permutation. Published connecting time (428.8 core-hours) is multiplied by f = 2 (H4) and converted at heuristic R = 2^25.400 units/core-second (H7 microarch model). Preprocessing charges priced extensions 2^48.585 plus an explicit 2^48 unit core-generation upper bound for TrailCoreInKernelAtC / unstated GPU step (H6) — total T_trail = 2^49.322. Every connector retry and enumerated failure is included.
Success probability 0.44 is for the budget-truncated algorithm with K = 22 under H1-H4, H8, H9 (proof Section 5: 0.4414). Without H8/H9 the Markov-only fallback is about 2^54.18 (not claimed).
The nominal reference identifier is required metadata and does not assert an improvement or Pareto dominance.

heuristics.statement: A pair from a successful p = 8 connector for hard-wired trail core No. 3 collides on the full 256-bit digest with probability at least 2^-37.22 (exhaustive Markov sum over 2^19 alpha4). Published 2^-36.70 is not used.
heuristics.scope: Rounds 3-5 of core No. 3 for SHA3-256 digest lanes 0-3.
heuristics.extrapolation: Markov independent-round model on p = 8 connector outputs with random fixed bits.
heuristics.limitations: No p = 8 experiment (F-NO-P8-VALIDATION / F5). Single published p = 4 collision lacks resolution to separate 2^-37.22 from 2^-36.70.

heuristics.statement: Within one 2^32-pair connector space, collision count is close to Poisson with s = 0.02647. Cross-space independence is exact by fresh M0/coins.
heuristics.scope: Each successful connector space in Section 4.
heuristics.extrapolation: Nonlinear rounds 3-5 on a 32-dimensional affine space behave like independent pair trials for collision counting.

heuristics.statement: Successful p = 8 connector attempts for core No. 3 return DF >= 33 (rank drop at most 4 from a DF = 37 parent; G7 slope predicts ~34).
heuristics.extrapolation: From one published DF = 37 instance at p = 4 to typical random p = 8 attempts.
heuristics.limitations: F3-dimension-transfer: observed DF = 37 is one instance; rank fact alone does not force every random parent to have DF = 37. Failed DF < 33 attempts are absorbed by H4.

heuristics.statement: Expected work E[C] for one successful p = 8 connector (DF >= 33), failures included, is at most f * Tc with f = 2 (857.6 core-hours), i.e. at most mu = 2^46.961 units under H7.
heuristics.scope: Connector Algorithms 1-3 for core No. 3 with c+p = 520 and random fixed bits.
heuristics.extrapolation: From one published p = 4 timing; f = 1.25 (G7) x 1.6 (one-sample factor).
heuristics.limitations: F-CONNECTOR-EXPECTATION-TAIL: single p = 4 sample + two-point slope do not prove an expected p = 8 upper bound. f = 2 is a declared heuristic pad, not a confidence interval.

heuristics.statement: The difference system can keep zero difference on all 8 padding bits as well as capacity.
heuristics.scope: Difference phase of the connector for core No. 3 at p = 8.
heuristics.extrapolation: From published beta0 already zero on the padding byte (Section 3) and slack counting.
heuristics.limitations: Counting argument only; not re-solved at p = 8.

heuristics.statement: Step P costs at most 2^49.322 units including priced extensions (2^48.585) and an explicit 2^48 unit upper bound for TrailCoreInKernelAtC core generation plus the unstated GPU step, and outputs hard-wired core No. 3 by fingerprint.
heuristics.scope: Preprocessing Step P in Section 4 and Section 6.
heuristics.extrapolation: Generation bound is a conservative unpublished-cost envelope (G6 gives no time); extensions use leaf primitive bounds.
heuristics.limitations: If true generation exceeds 2^48 units, the claim is void. Starting-core cardinality 2^13 is an assumption for extension pricing only; selection no longer depends on global min over that set.

heuristics.statement: One CPU core-second of the published connector corresponds to at most about 2^25.400 target-compression units under the microarchitectural model 5e9 cycles/s x 6 instr/cycle x 2 primitives/instr / 1355.
heuristics.scope: Conversion of Tc wall-clock into collision-frontier-v5 units for Phase A.
heuristics.extrapolation: Prices all connector wall-clock (LA, memory traffic, retries) at that primitive rate.
heuristics.limitations: F-WALLCLOCK-CONVERSION: Keccak throughput quotes are not a demonstrated upper bound on v5-priced LA ops. H7 is heuristic; the microarch rate exceeds paper G5 five-round equivalents (~2^24.263), increasing the charged cost.

heuristics.statement: Work C to obtain one successful connector attempt is a geometric number of i.i.d. attempt costs whose tail is no heavier than the equal-cost or exponential models used in Section 5 with K = 22 and B_A = 23 mu.
heuristics.scope: Phase A hard-cap success analysis with K = 22.
heuristics.extrapolation: From G2 retry structure and i.i.d. fresh M0/coins.
heuristics.limitations: F2-H8-tail-support: no attempt timings; variable attempt costs may have heavier tails. Metadata matches operative K = 22 (fixes F4-h8-k-parameter-mismatch).

heuristics.statement: Conditional on a connector success with DF >= 33 completed within B_A, the collision indicator of the emitted 2^32-pair space is independent of the work spent to obtain that success, so completed spaces remain Bernoulli-s trials for the hard-cap bound.
heuristics.scope: Section 5 success theorem relating budget-truncated completions to Pr >= 1-exp(-K s)-(1-s)^M.
heuristics.extrapolation: Separates attempt-level independence (fresh coins) from within-success work/mark independence.
heuristics.limitations: F1-budget-selection-dependence: untested. If high-work successes have atypical collision propensity, the bound may fail; Markov-only fallback ~2^{mark:.2f} is not claimed.

heuristics.statement: Peak memory of Step P + connector + enumeration is at most 2^40 bytes, covering KeccakTools generation structures, retained candidates, traversal state, code, and working tables.
heuristics.extrapolation: Conservative allowance above prior unsupported 2^34 figure.
heuristics.limitations: F-MEMORY-ALLOWANCE / F2-unsupported-memory-allowance: not measured on an implementation; structured as H10 rather than a silent assumption.
